findings: RankOneMetric uses the actual ContinuousLinearMap operator norm. Its residual identities prove the sharp unit-vector projector formula, including the dependent-vector case; lower bound is evaluation at u and upper bound uses the residual Cauchy-Schwarz estimate.

SixColumnMetric wraps plain Fin6 functions in the actual Mathlib PiLp 2 carrier, whose norm is the Euclidean norm. I compared its specialized sum-inner-product instance directly with pinned Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/PiL2.lean lines 83-105; it is the same construction and all instance fields are kernel checked. No sup norm is substituted.

columnProjector_matrix_entry proves literal matrix entries u_i conjugate(u_j). columnL2_norm_sq and columnL2_inner prove the concrete sum of squared moduli and conventional conjugate-first inner product.

RepeatedProjectorMetric consumes the actual normalized columns and their proved unit mass, turning the checked scalar infidelity inequalities into operator-norm bounds without an abstract metric premise.

NormalizedColumnMetric divides the actual matrix columns by sqrt6 and proves mass1 from actual unit-modulus entries. Its per-column projector distance is bounded by a true double-sum Frobenius error, using only nonnegative terms.
RowPermutationMetric proves mass and overlap invariance for an actual Equiv.Perm Fin6, then proves operator-distance equality for unit columns. No maximality assertion is transported.
axiom_audit: Every theorem and the concrete inner-product instance is printed in its successful receipt; standard propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.
scope_limits: Review covers these five typed metric components, not the final physical assembly or ClusterTube theorem.
No sector closure, supplier-box closure, or admission promotion is inferred.
